claims.text: A graded Mo-based refractory alloy can be used as an interlayer between W and CuCrZr.
The graded Mo-based interlayer will enhance the bond between W and CuCrZr.
Directly bonded W and CuCrZr typically form brittle intermetallic compounds.
Directly bonded W and CuCrZr exhibit high residual stresses because of thermal-expansion mismatch.
Chemical incompatibility contributes to problems in directly bonded W/CuCrZr joints.
Tailored additions of refractory elements to a predominantly Mo interlayer can chemically bridge W and CuCrZr.
Fusion-reactor components face high temperatures, severe irradiation, and neutron exposure.
The proposed joint must withstand severe thermal cycling in fusion-reactor service.
The interlayer can be compositionally graded from a W-compatible side to a CuCrZr-compatible side.
The compositional gradient will provide a gradual thermal-expansion transition between W and CuCrZr.
The compositional gradient will reduce abrupt chemical interactions at the W/CuCrZr interface.
Reducing abrupt chemical interactions will suppress brittle intermetallic formation.
A smooth thermal and chemical transition will alleviate interfacial stresses.
The graded interlayer will improve the mechanical strength and durability of the W/CuCrZr joint.
The graded interlayer will lower residual stresses relative to direct or non-graded joints.
The graded interlayer will enhance resistance to failure during thermal and irradiation cycling.
Conventional direct bonds or non-graded interlayers typically exhibit brittle interfacial phases and higher stress concentrations.
Irradiation doses or temperature gradients beyond the interlayer's stability range may limit its effectiveness.
The long-term behavior of the graded interlayer under prolonged irradiation and diffusion-induced compositional change is uncertain.
